title: Finite-coefficient inputs detect natural compact-support comparisons
statement: Let l,E,k,X,Y,f,c and the two compact-support functors be as in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] and [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action]. Suppose two natural transformations between the actual completed proper/open functor restricted to integral constructible inputs and the recorded integral compact-support functor followed by ambient inclusion agree at every constructible integral input which is isomorphic to the restriction of a derived complex over one positive finite quotient of the completed coefficient ring [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Then the natural transformations agree. No finite scalar-reduction equality is assumed in this statement.

source.place: Adic density/naturality on the strict resolving category in the parent rigidity plan; Bhatt--Scholze 6.7.6--6.7.7; Stacks 0941, 0F7J

proof.text: PROVED PART: finite-coefficient-input agreement is equivalent to agreement after every finite derived scalar extension, by lem-qcqs-compact-support-torsion-input-finite-evaluation. The forward implication makes the restricted quotient input constructible using the principal reduction triangle, then cancels the scalar-adjunction unit after transporting its explicit retraction through the natural compact-support reduction isomorphism. The converse uses the proved torsion coefficient action and injectivity of the scalar Hom transpose into a restricted target. The assigned assertion still needs the same natural-transformation rigidity in either formulation.

PROVED ADDITIONAL CASE (H2): finite shifted Hom groups in the output reduction towers imply detection by the Milnor injection. The generic finite-coefficient etale Hom proof gives this finiteness over any algebraically closed base field, not just the algebraic closure of a finite field. Thus the original detection statement is now proved with the additional hypothesis IsAlgClosed k. The arbitrary-field theorem and its existing hole are unchanged.

UNCOMPLETED PLAN (the coherent-lift objection below remains): Use augmented strict quotient-tensor systems of complete inputs and simultaneous flat-term K-flat resolutions. Each restricted finite quotient is a constructible integral input, so the hypothesis identifies the comparisons on those resolving inputs. Naturality along augmentation and resolution comparison maps identifies their universal counit comparisons before evaluation. The reduction/total-limit Hom transpose is unique; descend its equality through the resolving localization and conjugate by the recorded projection-normalized gamma. No ordinary categorical limit universal property or joint monicity of derived evaluations is asserted.

proof_origin.place: Formalized the quotient-input and finite-evaluation portion; retained the disputed coherent-system finish without a new sorry or changed statement
proof_origin.review_note: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the proposed strict resolving-diagram argument requires a coherent lift of arbitrary ordinary natural transformations, not supplied by the stated hypotheses or cited declarations. The scalar adjunction only detects whole derived-system maps. The finite-field Milnor injection has additional base-field hypotheses. No counterexample is claimed; the statement and existing hole are retained for independent mathematical review.
proof_origin.remaining: The torsion-input and finite-evaluation agreement hypotheses have been proved equivalent. Equality of the original natural transformations remains unproved over an arbitrary base field; changing between these two hypotheses does not reduce that remaining rigidity obligation.
proof_origin.additional_note: H2 proves the actual detection conclusion over every algebraically closed original base field, with no new holes. The existing arbitrary-field assertion and coherent-lift dispute remain; no equivalence of hypotheses is split off again.
